title: 🗺️ Reference Map
intro: Coverage of the Software Engineering Delivery Model 2026 by AgentCase, one row per reference subchapter: a short summary, the coverage status, and a direct link to the AgentCase section that carries it.
footnote: Coverage of the six-part reference model. Click a section to jump to the AgentCase tab that carries it. See the full gap analysis for detail.
help: Maps AgentCase against its source document — the

— one row per reference subchapter. It answers "does this tool actually implement the reference model, or just borrow its vocabulary?", and it answers it per chapter, including where the answer is no.
— the reference section, in the reference's own numbering.
— what that chapter requires, in one line.
— covered · partial · not covered. Partial and absent rows are shown, not hidden; the counters at the top are the honest tally.
— straight into the AgentCase section that carries it, so a claim of coverage can be checked immediately rather than taken on trust.
, it is the credibility artefact for a client who knows the reference model — it shows the tool was built against a published method, not invented.
, the partial and uncovered rows are the product backlog: they are where the model still asserts rather than derives.
. When a new phase or section lands, this map is the place that has to be updated for the claim to stay true — a stale reference map is worse than none.

rows.summary: Vision for an agentic software factory and the L1–L4 maturity scale (Ad-hoc Assistance → Autonomous Organization). AgentCase maps L-levels to the adoption ramp, vFTE share and AI-authorization, with objective L→L transition gates.
rows.label: FTE / vFTE (maturity mapping)

rows.summary: Three engagement contexts (Capgemini infra / client infra / staff augmentation) set the capacity to control the delivery system. Project eligibility combines a six-prerequisite gate with a pillar × SDLC potential matrix.
rows.label: Eligibility & Abaques

rows.summary: Three TJM pricing models (Effort & Tools, AI-augmented humans, mixed teams / agentshore) and the T0/T1/T2 commitment calendar (commit gains only once measured). AgentCase prices all models client-vs-margin.
rows.label: Commercial model

rows.summary: Spec-Driven Development (spec as primary artifact), the six-layer agent stack, four memories / living metamodel, and the model & sovereignty socle. AgentCase turns SDD and harness readiness into levers that cut the verification tax.
rows.label: Maturity & Measurement (SDD)

rows.summary: The harness as the unit of configuration, secure local setup and distribution at scale (≈88% of pilots never industrialise). Largely playbook; the pilot-mortality risk is carried by AgentCase, plus the AI-BOM.
rows.label: Risk & Compliance

rows.summary: The merge becomes the bottleneck; teams recompose into pods of 2–4 in a diamond shape (a team of 10 → ~3 pods of ~3), with transverse roles and an AI Office, scaling under AI-Native SAFe.
rows.label: Operating model

rows.summary: The 90/10 skill shift, the knowledge-debt risk and the answer of deliberate learning: preceptorship 3:1–5:1, review-first, coaching. AgentCase models a declining coaching curve and the autonomy-weaning tiers.
rows.label: Maturity & Measurement (coaching)

rows.summary: People are the real failure factor (≈40% fear job loss). Address fear, do not over-sell (perceived vs real gain), and watch human indicators. AgentCase carries the HRI, the human early-warning indicators and the verification tax.
rows.label: AI Readiness (HRI)

rows.summary: The pilot is the tipping point, run as a product (it delivers a factory, not an app): DEC → HOW → BLD, frozen harness, demonstration milestones, fail-fast. AgentCase sizes pilot duration and cost.
rows.label: Program & Completeness (pilot)

rows.summary: Teach to fish: a progressive autonomy scale with deliberate support decay — intensive coaching → on-demand → self-service → community of practice — sustained by champions.
rows.label: Maturity & Measurement (autonomy)

rows.summary: Discover → Prove → Scale, in two volets: internal Capgemini capability (A, 50→200→500) and client deployment (B). AgentCase surfaces the client roadmap and the internal capability ramp.
rows.label: 🤝 Engage (client deployment roadmap)

rows.summary: AI code quality is not a given (×1.57–×1.75 more issues). The human answers for the system they designed; tripartite governance, non-bypassable gates, enlarged DoD and an AI-BOM. AgentCase carries the supervision matrix, quality premium and gates.
rows.label: Risk & Compliance

rows.summary: Three complementary frameworks (EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001) and an agentic risk register (prompt injection, MCP supply chain, secrets, vendor lock-in, hallucination, knowledge debt). AgentCase ships the register and an AI-Act tier classifier.
rows.label: Risk & Compliance

rows.summary: IP of deliverables, confidentiality and sovereignty synthesised per engagement context; purely AI-generated code has uncertain protection; never send confidential context to an unmastered model. AgentCase gives a per-context synthesis.
rows.label: Program & Completeness (IP)

rows.summary: Addressable gain ≠ net gain: Abaque A (addressable per phase) × Abaque B (captured by maturity) minus the verification tax — the ~10% net productivity paradox. AgentCase makes both abaques and the tax first-class.
rows.label: Eligibility & Abaques

rows.summary: COCOMO/KLOC breaks down; estimate from spec × capacity × supervision × tokens. FinOps GenAI: lowest total cost (tokens + review), not lowest token bill; caching removes up to ~90% of input cost.
rows.label: Program & Completeness (token cache)

rows.summary: DORA is no longer enough: steer four families — DORA + SPACE + AI signals + human indicators — with the change-failure-rate guardrail and value beyond billable staffing. AgentCase carries the four-family socle.
rows.label: Maturity & Measurement (socle)
